turns.text: Hey Lloyd, did you see the news about Warp? They finally open-sourced their repository, which led to a massive surge in GitHub stars from around 20,000 to over 60,000 in roughly three months. Pretty wild growth.
That is indeed a significant jump. Open-sourcing often drives that kind of community engagement and visibility. Have you tried installing it from the new repo yet?
Not yet, my build environment is still acting up. I'm trying to get Rust up to date, but cargo keeps throwing errors about missing dependencies.
That can be frustrating. Did you run `cargo clean` before updating? Sometimes stale artifacts cause those dependency conflicts.
I did, but it didn't help. I think it's an issue with my global config. I'll dig into it later. Anyway, back to Warp, the UI looks much snappier than the old version.
Performance improvements are usually a key selling point for new terminal emulators. It's good to see the community validating that speed.
Yeah. Also, it's raining again here. I need to make sure I take the umbrella if I head out for lunch.
Stay dry! Let me know if you need help troubleshooting that Rust config later.
Lloyd, I've been testing Warp Terminal for the last week. It has really grown into an agentic development environment. The AI commands are surprisingly useful for refactoring code.
That's a major shift from just being a faster terminal. Integrating agentic features changes the workflow significantly. How is the learning curve for those AI commands?
It's manageable. I spent the morning fixing a bug in my Python script. The auto-completion for imports is saving me a lot of time.
Efficiency gains in import management are a nice quality-of-life improvement. Did you encounter any latency issues with the agentic features?
No, it's pretty responsive. I'm actually ordering a new mechanical keyboard today to match the aesthetic. The clicky switches are supposed to help my focus.
A new keyboard can definitely boost productivity and comfort. Hope the switches are worth the hype.
I think so. Anyway, the agentic nature of Warp is what sold me. It feels like pair programming with a fast robot.
An interesting analogy. It seems you're adapting well to this new paradigm.
